_README: Source map for the Reddit digest, organized by the buckets defined in taste.md. Entries marked DRAFT are starting candidates that haven't been vetted in a live run yet — check them against taste.md's filters (especially the slugfest and petty-gripe rules) before trusting them long-term.

daily.label: Trades, on-the-ground practice, emerging tech
daily.notes: Drawn straight from your existing follow list — these already match the practitioner-discussion / on-the-ground framing well. OP is often a photo or a one-line question; anchor on the title and surface the substantive replies underneath.

daily.label: Market sentiment, trade conditions, real estate economics
daily.notes: DRAFT. Your follow list doesn't include a dedicated real-estate-economics sub, so these are starting guesses. Caution: r/RealEstate skews toward individual-buyer anxiety threads ('should I waive inspection') — exactly the petty-gripe pattern taste.md says to filter. Worth checking whether it clears the bar after a week of real output, or whether something more trade-press-flavored fits better.

daily.label: Climate, ecology, conservation, climate justice, human rights
daily.notes: DRAFT, deliberately cast wide per 'open to anything.' Sustainability/Sustainable/Permaculture overlap with the trades bucket — that's fine, a good thread can surface in either. Same slugfest/outrage filter from taste.md applies here, probably more than anywhere else.

daily.label: Political economy — academic register, not the slugfest
daily.notes: DRAFT, aimed at the 'academic, not slugfest' framing specifically. r/badeconomics is more rigorous than its name suggests (it exists to dissect bad arguments using real theory). Filter for evidence-and-structure threads; topical overlap with a culture-war fight is not the same as fit.

daily.label: Sci-fi book & film recommendations
daily.notes: DRAFT. Target recommendation-shaped threads specifically ('what should I read/watch next', 'looking for something like X'), not general sci-fi news or discourse — that distinction matters more than the subreddit choice here.

seasonal.label: Booker Prize & Nobel Prize in Literature
windows: Nobel Prize in Literature: announced early October
seasonal.notes: Explicitly NOT the Pulitzer. Match on keywords ('Booker', 'Nobel') around these windows rather than following day-to-day — most days would come up empty, then flood around announcements.

seasonal.label: IPCC assessments & major economic reports
examples: major Fed releases / significant economic data drops
seasonal.notes: Check for and surface discussion around known release windows; same evidence-over-hot-take filter from taste.md applies to the discussion threads these spawn.

from_your_follow_list_not_yet_placed.note: Subreddits from your historical follow dump that don't map cleanly onto a bucket above. Some look like deliberate 'weight down' calls from taste.md (financialindependence/personalfinance/Frugal — the lottery-ideology pattern); others (dad, Dogtraining, reactivedogs, Huntingdogs, redletterchristians, Darkroom, Lightning, CLOUDS, Kiteboarding, Sup, mathteachers, TheGreatLoop, ThingsIWishIKnew, treehouse, treehouses, declutter, minimalism, minimalist, NoLawns, fucklawns) just look like personal-life/hobby follows that may not be 'newspaper'-shaped at all. Flagging rather than guessing — say the word if any of these should be folded into a bucket.
